heading: Known limitations and gotchas
text: - **`move` reports a changed element, not always the moved one.** The one-line result `changed <fqn> (in components)` names an element whose position changed, which can be the sibling that shifted. `move <fqn> --json` prints `reordered <fqn> in <list>` for the moved element, and `status` lists each unsaved move as `move <fqn> index=n` or `after=<fqn>`. Check the final order with a query (for example `graphql` on the container's `components`); `discard --force` drops a wrong reorder, together with all other unsaved edits.
evidence: CLI run on a Sandbox copy: `move <view>::note --after <view>::name` printed `changed ...::code (in components)`; `move ... --json` summary `reordered ...::note in components`; `status` showed `move ... after=...`

heading: Known limitations and gotchas
text: - **`postCallAccessNavigation` cannot be cleared.** It is an attribute of the `OperationForm` (ui element) only. `update <operationForm> --unset postCallAccessNavigation` is refused (`cannot be cleared on OperationForm <name>`), `--clear` fails (`not a list`) and `--set postCallAccessNavigation=` is not an allowed value. Set it only when the target is final; to remove it, delete the `OperationForm` and place it again with `update <container> --add feature --feature <operation>`. The allowed values are the accesses whose target type matches the operation's output; `--set` lists them on error.
evidence: CLI run on a Sandbox copy (update on OperationForm: unset/clear/set-empty). `move --index` on an ActionGroup in a view and on menu items worked in the same run (not reproduced: see note); first-pass reproduction of the index claim failed, so it is left out.

heading: Known limitations and gotchas
text:
- **Place actions with `update <container> --add feature`.** The container must exist and be given by its exact FQN; `Container not found: <fqn>` means that FQN does not exist yet (create the `ActionGroup` first with `create -t ActionGroup --ns <viewFqn> -n <group>`). The operation must be a member of the container's transfer object: for a relation table (`<view>::<relation>`) it is an operation of the relation's target transfer object, otherwise the error is `'<op>' is not a feature of <TO> placeable here`, followed by the placeable features.
  - Table actions: `update <viewFqn>::<relation> --add feature --feature <operation> --as rowAction|tableAction|bulkAction`. This creates a `TableOperation` with a nested `OperationForm`.
  - A direct placement in an `ActionGroup`: `update <viewFqn>::<group> --add feature --feature <operation>` creates the `OperationForm` inside the group.
  - On a view, `--as action` is not a role (`valid field`).
evidence: CLI run on a Sandbox copy: `update <view>::<relation> --add feature --feature act --as rowAction` created TableOperation; `update <view>::actions --add feature --feature doIt` created OperationForm; `update <view>::nothing ...` gave Container not found

heading: 8. `TabularReferenceField` rules by relation shape
text:
The CLI enforces the `representationComponent` value for the bound relation and lists the allowed values when a value is refused (`'<v>' is not an allowed value of 'representationComponent' ...; allowed: [...]`). Observed on a mapped relation:

| `upper` | `relationKind` | Allowed values |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `AGGREGATION` | `table` |
| 1 | `ASSOCIATION` | `table`, `button` |
| -1 | `ASSOCIATION` | `table`, `button`, `tag`, `card` |
| -1 | `AGGREGATION` | `table`, `tag`, `card` |

Change `relationKind` first, then set `representationComponent`; read the allowed list from the error message instead of guessing.
evidence: CLI run on a Sandbox copy: update <view>::<relation> --set representationComponent=<v> for each combination; create --schema lists representationComponent only as `string`

heading: 17. Reference-derived elements, custom components and capability rules
text:
### Placing a feature into a relation table

A column of a relation table belongs to the target transfer object of the relation. Address the table element, not the page: `update <viewFqn>::<relation> --add feature --feature <member>` (the member is a feature of the relation's target type). On the page element the same name fails with `'<member>' is not a feature of <PageTO> placeable here`. The error also fires when the member is already placed; the `valid` list that follows shows only the features that can still be placed. `fill <TO>` already places a column for every member.
evidence: CLI run on a Sandbox copy: `update <view> --add feature --feature name` and `update <view>::<relation> --add feature --feature name` after `fill`

heading: 17. Reference-derived elements, custom components and capability rules
text:
### Embedded tables in a view and `isEager`

`isEager` is not an ESM attribute and cannot be set in the model. The transformation sets it on the generated `ui` table: it is `true` when the relation is an aggregation or a composition, or when the page that holds the table is a Form. An eager table keeps its rows in memory (the owner's data) and never calls the server for paging, sorting or filtering; any other table is lazy (server side, paged). To embed a table in a view, place a to-many `TabularReferenceField` with `representationComponent=table` on the view and use `AGGREGATION` or `COMPOSITION` for an eager table.

heading: 17. Reference-derived elements, custom components and capability rules
text:
### Rows of an embedded table are saved with the page

A table over an aggregation or composition relation is eager: its rows live in the owner's data. Creating a row from it opens the create dialog as a draft (`isDraft`) and adds the row to the owner's data; nothing is sent to the server until the page's Update (save) action runs. A test that adds or edits such rows must click the page's Update button afterwards. Rows of a lazy table (association) are created on the server at once.

heading: 9. `hiddenBy` / `enabledBy` / `requiredBy`
text: **Hiding a generated action.** Add a `TRANSIENT` or `DERIVED` boolean `DataMember` to the transfer object that owns the action, then set `hiddenBy` on the `OperationForm`, `ActionButton` or `ActionGroup`: `update <viewFqn>::<action> --set hiddenBy=<TO>.<booleanMember>`. The CLI accepts only boolean members of the owner transfer object (`'<x>' is not an allowed value`, followed by the valid list). The action is hidden while the boolean is `true`. `TableOperation` has no `hiddenBy`; set it on its nested `OperationForm`.
evidence: CLI run on a Sandbox copy: create --schema lists hiddenBy on OperationForm, ActionButton, ActionGroup and not on TableOperation; `update <view>::doIt --set hiddenBy=<TO>.hideIt` accepted, a non-boolean member refused

heading: Collection Functions
text:
| `!head()` / `!heads(i \| key)` | Instance / Collection | `!head(i \| key)` returns one item with the smallest `key` (`DESC`: the largest). `!heads(i \| key)` returns **all** items that share that smallest (or, with `DESC`, largest) key, so it is the tie set, not the first `n` items. There is no top-N function: sort, then limit through paging (`rowsPerPage`, `limit`). |
| `!tail()` / `!tails(i \| key)` | Instance / Collection | The mirror of `head` / `heads` (largest key first). |
replace:
| `!head()` / `!heads(n)` | Instance / Collection | First item / first `n` items. Order is deterministic only after `!sort`. |
| `!tail()` / `!tails(n)` | Instance / Collection | Last item / last `n` items. |

heading: Widget Type Attributes
text: | `textWidget` | StringType | `TEXT`/`INPUT` | `TEXT` renders the value as plain text (`ui:Formatted`): no label, no input, no tooltip, optionally an icon. `INPUT` renders a labelled input (`ui:TextInput` or `ui:TextArea`). To keep the label on a read-only value, use `INPUT` on a read-only (derived) member. |
